title: Implement delay time controller with host timing pod and tap median
description:
Create Source/DSP/DelayTimeController.h and Source/DSP/DelayTimeController.cpp implementing delay-time mode resolution for the two voices.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/ (existing module style, include guards, namespace)
- Source/PluginProcessor.h (to confirm the processor is the only place that queries the host; DSP modules never query the host)
- CMakeLists.txt (source layout only; do NOT modify it in this task)

Required implementation:
1. Define in DelayTimeController.h the plain POD struct, verbatim in field order and types:
   struct HostTiming { double bpm; bool bpmValid; bool isPlaying; std::int64_t samplePosition; };
   The processor fills this once per block and passes it in. DSP modules must never call any host/playhead API.
2. Time modes:
   - Milliseconds: D_samples = Fs * T_ms / 1000.
   - HostSync: T_quarter = 60 / BPM; T = ratio * T_quarter. Divisions Whole (4.0), Half (2.0), Quarter (1.0), Eighth (0.5), Sixteenth (0.25), each with a dotted variant (x1.5) and a triplet variant (x2/3), expressed as ratios of a quarter note.
   - Tap: maintain a fixed K = 5 interval history in a fixed-size array (no dynamic allocation); the tempo is the median of the history. Intervals outside [100 ms, 3000 ms] are rejected and never enter the history.
3. BPM fallback: when bpmValid is false, retain the last valid BPM. If no valid BPM was ever received, fall back to 120 BPM. Never jump to zero, negative, or undefined delay.
4. Per-voice target: T_voice = T_base * ratio + fineOffset (in seconds). Modulation and stereo offsets are applied downstream, not here.
5. Transition requests: expose a small result/request type indicating whether a change should be rendered as Smooth or Bend, and issue such a request for large changes, including host-tempo jumps, scene changes, and profile changes. Do not use an ordinary linear smoother for large delay-time changes.
6. No allocation, locking, IO, string construction, or unbounded loops outside prepare().

The files must be standard C++20 only (<cmath>, <cstdint>, <array>, <algorithm>). Do NOT include any JUCE header.
acceptance_criteria: DelayTimeController.h defines struct HostTiming { double bpm; bool bpmValid; bool isPlaying; std::int64_t samplePosition; }
Milliseconds mode computes D_samples = Fs * T_ms / 1000 and HostSync computes T = ratio * (60 / BPM) with Whole, Half, Quarter, Eighth, Sixteenth plus dotted x1.5 and triplet x2/3 ratios
Tap mode stores a fixed K = 5 interval history in a fixed-size array, takes the median, and rejects intervals outside 100-3000 ms
When bpmValid is false the last valid BPM is retained, and 120 BPM is used if none was ever received
Per-voice target is computed as T_voice = T_base * ratio + fineOffset
The controller issues Smooth or Bend transition requests for large delay-time changes instead of using an ordinary linear smoother
No host or playhead API is called from DelayTimeController
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: include any JUCE header in DelayTimeController.h or DelayTimeController.cpp
call any host, playhead, or transport API from a DSP module
create or modify Source/DSP/FractionalDelay.*, Source/DSP/FeedbackController.*, or Source/DSP/DelayVoice.*
use std::vector or dynamic allocation for the tap history
